sources.citation: English Wikipedia 'Karolanos language' (raw wikitext 2026-09-17); Wikidata Q6373093.
sources.note: Stub; cites only Gonzaga 1988 (Philippine Studies 36(2):151-165, agrarian history, name 'Karul-an') and Lobel 2013. Nothing on phonology.

sources.citation: Sister-language audits already on file:../maga1264/Southern Binukidnon [mtw], same negative result);../sulo1237/Rentillo 2025 Dialectologia 34, Panay only);../mara1404 Kaufman & Himmelmann suprasegmentals chapter and Zorc 1993 accent overview; Zorc 1977 PL C-44 (../akla1241,../cebu1242).
sources.note: None of these contain any Negros Binukidnon/Karolanos data point; Zorc 1977's 36 Bisayan dialects include no Negros Bukidnon variety.

sources.citation: OLAC combined catalog. 2024. 'OLAC resources in and about the Northern Binukidnon language' (kyn), up-to-date 2024-12-11 (Wayback capture). http://www.language-archives.org/language/kyn
sources.note: Language descriptions listed: only the Glottolog 5.0 stub; other resources: Ethnologue and LINGUIST List stubs. No primary description of any kind exists in any OLAC archive.

sources.citation: Eberhard, Simons & Fennig (eds.). 2019. Ethnologue: Languages of the World, 22nd ed., entry 'Binukidnon, Northern' [kyn] (Wayback capture of free page).
sources.note: Alt. name Karolanos; 15,100 (2000); Negros Occidental, Kabankalan; 'Dialects: None known. Reportedly similar to Southern Binukidnon [mtw]'. Nothing on phonology.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.x languoid record karo1299 'Northern Binukidnon' (Negrosanon < Bisayan); langdoc: Lobel 2013 (MED wordlist_or_less), Ethnologue 17, ISO CR 2009-065; hh.bib grep for karolan|binukidnon|carol-an|negros bukidnon adds only Larena et al. 2021 PNAS (genetics).

Lobel, Jason William. 2013. Philippine and North Bornean languages: Issues in description, subgrouping, and reconstruction. PhD dissertation, University of Hawai'i at Manoa. xx+422 pp. http://hdl.handle.net/10125/101972
sources.note: All 10 passages naming Northern Binukidnon/NBUK extracted: p.3 (listed among 'previously-undocumented languages' documented), Map 1.8 key p.24, p.39 fn.5 (Negros Binukidnon languages 'do not immediately subgroup with the migrant Cebuano and Ilonggo languages surrounding them, except as members of the larger Bisayan subgroup'), Table 2.11 p.52 (NBUK case markers), p.63 (Inata speakers also use N. Binukidnon), p.249 fn.21, p.273 fn.33 (Negros Binukidnon keeps inherited *h in codas), p.341, p.379 fn.19. No phonology section and no statement about stress/accent for either Negros Binukidnon langua…

sources.citation: Lobel, Jason (with William Hall, SIL Philippines). 2009. ISO 639-3 Change Request 2009-065: rename [kyn] 'Karolanos' -> 'Binukidnon, Northern' (adopted 2010-01-18). SIL International. 5 pp.
sources.note: Nothing linguistic. p.2: 'There to date have been no publications about this language (wether under the names "Karolanos", "Carol-an", "Binukidnon" or "Bukidnon"...), so the first publications to mention this language will be the Lobel dissertation and a separate paper Lobel is writing on these languages.' Spoken 'throughout the northern two-thirds of Negros Is.'

sources.citation: Lobel, Jason William. Unpublished field data on Northern and Southern Binukidnon (Negros), 2005-2007 (the 'separate paper Lobel is writing on these languages' announced in ISO CR 2009-065, p.2; absent from his publication list through 2020).
